item.title: Canada’s Anne Carson wins Nobel literature prize
item.description:
The Nobel Prize in Literature was awarded on Thursday to Canadian poet Anne Carson, an essayist and classicist who brings a modern twist to mysticism and antiquity in her writings about love, desire and despair.
The 76-year-old was honored “for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature,” the Swedish Academy said.
The permanent secretary of the Swedish Academy, Ingrid Carlberg, said she had briefly spoken to Carson.
“We didn’t have so much time to speak. All she had time to tell me was that she is for the moment in Iceland, where she’s listening to the wind.”
“She was taken by surprise, but very happy. I could hear that in her voice.”
The Academy said almost all her literary production “has centered upon the intersection between the philologist’s obsession with words and the poet’s desire for new meaning.”
It singled out her poem “Nox,” printed on one continuous sheet of paper in homage to her dead brother, as “an unforgettable work.”
Carson has been mentioned as a possible Nobel laureate for years.
Many literary critics had predicted the award would go to a woman this year, given the frequent criticism directed at the Academy over the overrepresentation of Western white men among its picks.
There have been just 19 women laureates out of 122 since the Nobel Prize in Literature was first awarded in 1901.
A 2018 sex assault scandal left the Academy in tatters and more than half of its 18 members were replaced.
Since then, every other literature laureate has been a woman.
Last year, the award went to Hungary’s Laszlo Krasznahorkai, whose works explore themes of postmodern dystopia.
The Nobel Prize comes with a diploma, a gold medal and a $1.2 million prize sum.
Carson will receive the award from King Carl XVI Gustaf in Stockholm on December 10, the anniversary of the 1896 death of scientist and prize creator Alfred Nobel.

item.title: US-Bangladesh trade: Imports surge while exports drop
item.description:
While Bangladesh's ready-made garment exports to the US market have declined, imports from the country into Bangladesh are growing rapidly.
In the first six months of this year, Bangladesh's product imports from the United States grew by more than 113%.
Analysis of Bangladesh Bank's country-wise import data reveals that during the January–June period of 2026, Bangladesh imported goods worth $1.8962 billion from the United States.
Among this, goods worth $605.6 million were imported during the January–March period.
In the April–June period, that figure surged to $1.2906 billion. In other words, within a span of just three months, imports grew by 113.11%.
On the other hand, Bangladesh's readymade garment exports to the US market continue to exhibit a downward trend.
According to data from the US Office of Textiles and Apparel (Otexa), US garment imports from Bangladesh fell by 4.43% during the January–August period of this year, dropping to $5.39 billion.
However, looking at August as an individual month, Bangladesh's garment exports increased by 11.15% compared to the same month of the previous year.
As a result, while pressure is mounting on Bangladesh's main export item, RMG, in the US market, imports of energy, cotton, agricultural commodities, and other goods from that country are rising.
This has reignited discussions regarding the balance of trade relations between the two countries.
Imports more than double in three months
According to Bangladesh Bank data, the highest imports from the United States during the April–June period were petroleum products, bitumen, and other mineral fuels and oil products.
Import expenditure in this sector stood at $775.2 million. In contrast, expenditure in this sector during the January–March period was only $135.5 million.
Additionally, during the April–June period, $142.6 million worth of cotton, $104.1 million worth of iron and steel, $47.8 million worth of food grains, and $72.9 million worth of soybeans and animal feed were imported from the United States.
Measuring and testing equipment worth $21.9 million, electrical equipment worth $19.1 million, and plastic items worth $18.5 million were also imported during this timeframe.
Business leaders state that alongside the new trade agreement, factors such as product quality, supply assurance, and shifting international market dynamics are driving the increase in imports from the US.
The upward trend in imports from the United States has become more pronounced following the signing of the new 'Agreement on Reciprocal Trade' between Bangladesh and the US.
Under this agreement, Bangladesh committed to purchasing energy, agricultural commodities, cotton, and other goods from the United States.
According to Bangladesh Bank data, Bangladesh's imports from the United States rose to $3.5929 billion in FY26, compared to nearly $2.72 billion in the previous fiscal.
This indicates a significant year-on-year increase in imports.
A major catalyst for further import growth from the United States could be aircraft. Biman Bangladesh Airlines has reached agreements to purchase a total of 25 aircraft from the US manufacturer Boeing.
Out of these, the deal for 14 aircraft is valued at approximately $3.7 billion.
Later, agreements were made to acquire an additional 11 aircraft. Consequently, aircraft imports are expected to add substantial figures to Bangladesh's trade transactions with the US in the coming years, along with increased imports of aircraft spare parts, maintenance, and related services.
RMG declining
While imports from the US are expanding rapidly, the picture for Bangladesh's garment exports to the US market is less promising.
Otexa data indicates that overall US garment imports fell by 7.42% during the January–August period to $49.08 billion.
Import volume decreased by 8.98%, although the average unit price increased by 1.71%.
During this period, the value of US garment imports from China dropped by 29.39% and from India by 26.44%.
Imports from Pakistan fell by 3.83% and from Vietnam by 0.76%.
Conversely, imports increased by 2.58% from Indonesia and 6.91% from Cambodia.
For Bangladesh, import value fell by 4.43%, while volume declined by 2.75%. Simultaneously, the average unit price of Bangladeshi garments dropped by 1.73%.
During the first two months of the current fiscal year, Bangladesh's import expenditure grew faster than its export earnings.
In the July–August period, import spending rose by 12.1% to $12.2 billion, while export earnings grew by 5.8% to $8.38 billion.
As a result, the trade deficit widened by 29% during this period to $3.82 billion.
China and India continue to dominate Bangladesh's import market.
In FY25, Bangladesh imported approximately $18.19 billion worth of goods from China and around $9.62 billion from India, compared to $2.72 billion from the United States.

item.title: Minister Anee expects new Ganges water sharing treaty before December 12
item.description:
Water Resources Minister Shahiduddin Chowdhury Anee Thursday expressed hope that a new Ganges water sharing treaty with India would be signed before December 12 this year.
"Restoring the guarantee clause, as in the 1977 agreement, is one of Bangladesh's top priorities in the new treaty," Anee told reporters after a seminar titled "Rethinking the Future of Water: Youth Leadership, Justice and Cooperation," organized by Bangladesh Institute of International and Strategic Studies (BIISS).
The minister said the existing 30-year agreement would expire on December 12. "A five-year agreement signed in 1977 during the tenure of then president Ziaur Rahman contained a guarantee clause but the provision was dropped when the new treaty was signed in 1996."
"We must conclude a new Ganges water treaty before December 12," Anee said, adding that Bangladesh and India are working regularly through the Joint Rivers Commission (JRC).
"Based on meetings between the two countries, Bangladesh is optimistic that the new treaty will be finalized ahead of the deadline,” said the minister.
The minister also said work on the Padma Barrage would become visible between January and March next year.
The government is also moving ahead with a plan to complete the feasibility study of the Teesta multipurpose project and begin main construction in 2027, he added.
Describing the Padma Barrage and the Teesta Master Plan as mega projects of great importance, Anee said about one-third of the country's population would benefit once they are implemented.
The Padma Barrage project has already been approved by the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC), he added.
"We hope the work will become visible sometime in January, February or March next year," he said.
On the Teesta Master Plan, the minister said it was another major challenge for the government.
"The Teesta is a swift-flowing river, and people in the downstream areas have long been suffering because of water coming from upstream," he said, stressing the need for technical support from local and foreign experts.
He said discussions have been held with experts of Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET), who have been given responsibility in this regard, while many other local and international experts have also been consulted.
"The feasibility study of the Teesta project will begin very soon, and main work will start based on that study," he said, expressing hope that the necessary work, including the feasibility study, would be completed in 2027 and the main work launched in the same year.
Asked whether there was any foreign pressure or obstacle regarding the Padma Barrage and Teesta projects, the minister said people living along the Padma and the Teesta are citizens of Bangladesh.
"The interests and expectations of the people of the country are the biggest concern for me," he said, adding that the government's main goal was to work for their welfare.
Speaking about the progress of the Padma Barrage, he said the project's feasibility study took a long time, from 2004 to 2016, and was not implemented afterwards.
"The present government finalized the matter and started work within a few months of taking office," he said.
Noting that a study for a project as large as the Teesta cannot be completed overnight or in a month or two, the minister said previous authorities did not seek adequate technical support to finish the job.
"The present government wants to complete the necessary work on its own initiative and give the Teesta project a visible shape," he added.

item.title: Muktadir: Govt working to keep essentials affordable during Ramadan
item.description:
The government is taking various measures to ensure adequate supplies of essential commodities and reasonable prices for consumers during the upcoming Ramadan, Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir said on Thursday.
Initiatives are being taken to rationalize duties on fruits and dates, lower interest rates on bank loans for importing consumer goods, and remove obstacles to transportation and clearance of imported products, he said.
The minister made the comments while speaking at a discussion with traders and importers on ensuring the supply of essential commodities and market stability, organised by the Chittagong Chamber of Commerce and Industry (CCCI) at the World Trade Center in Chittagong.
The government will also continue regular market monitoring to prevent artificial crisis and unjustified price hikes, he said.
Regarding preparations for Ramadan, Muktadir said there are already sufficient supplies of essential commodities, including edible oil and sugar, while opening letters of credit (LCs) for imports is continuing as normal.
He said the government is working in coordination with relevant agencies to ensure smooth supply of essential goods throughout the year, including during Ramadan.
The minister stressed the need to reduce import costs to keep prices of essentials at a reasonable level.
The government is working to reduce the duty on the import of fruits, currently at 121%, to make them more affordable, he said, adding that a letter has also been sent to the National Board of Revenue (NBR) seeking a reduction in duties on dates.
Muktadir said he will discuss with the Bangladesh Bank governor the possibility of reducing interest rates on bank loans for importing consumer goods.
Responding to a question about unusually high fruit prices, he said selling imported oranges at Tk400-500 per kg even after payment of duties is unacceptable.
The minister, however, claimed that the price has fallen significantly following drives by the Directorate of National Consumer Rights Protection (DNCRP) and the administration.
“Artificial crisis or attempts to make excessive profits ahead of Ramadan or on any other occasion will not be tolerated,” he said, adding that market monitoring will continue throughout the year.
On reducing supply costs, Muktadir said initiatives have been taken to improve the efficiency of Chittagong Port and remove obstacles to the transport system with a view to bringing down the country's logistics costs from 16%.
He also highlighted several government initiatives to simplify business operations, including making the trade licence system fully online so that certificates can be downloaded from anywhere after payment of the prescribed fee.
The government is also working to modernise the Registrar of Joint Stock Companies and Firms (RJSC) on the model of Singapore and introduce a system for transferring shares remotely through facial recognition and fingerprint-based identity verification, the minister said.
He said the government is also considering making pre-shipment inspection (PSI) mandatory for imports of sodium sulphate, or synthetic salt, and bitumen to ensure quality and transparency.
Asked about the impact of the fuel price hike, Muktadir said the government had subsidised fuel for a long time and made a minimum price adjustment to maintain the country's financial balance.
He said steps are being taken to reduce duties on other imported products to prevent additional pressure on the market.
During the meeting, the business leaders assured the government that traders are fully prepared to maintain adequate supplies of essential commodities during Ramadan.
CCCI President Mohammad Amirul Haque, who chaired the meeting, said traders will ensure that there is no artificial crisis of major essentials, including lentils, chickpeas, wheat, edible oil and sugar.
He said they will regularly monitor market demand and stocks and coordinate with port and customs authorities to ensure smooth clearance of imported goods.
Describing Chittagong as the country's economic hub and an important centre for regional trade and logistics, Amirul called for ensuring a level playing field for businesses in the region.
He also reaffirmed the business community's commitment to conducting trade transparently and protecting consumer interests.
Khatunganj Trade and Industries Association President Abdus Salam urged customs, port and government agencies to strengthen coordination and avoid harassment of traders to ensure smooth supply during Ramadan.
He stressed the need for a cooperative environment for the import and clearance of goods.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,144 as four die in 24 hours
item.description:
Four more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Thursday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,144.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all four of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,040, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 104, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the four new suspected fatalities, the highest concentration was recorded in the Sylhet division with two deaths. At the district level, one casualty each was recorded in Sylhet, Sunamganj, Dhaka, and Khulna.
A total of 1,332 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Thursday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 201,625.
During the same period, 96 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 22,116.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 178,927 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 171,680 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: Dhaka, Jakarta discuss visa simplification, boosting trade
item.description:
Indonesian Vice Minister of Foreign Affairs Muhammad Anis Matta on Thursday met Prime Minister's adviser and spokesperson for the Prime Minister's Office Mahdi Amin to discuss simplifying visa and travel procedures and enhancing bilateral trade between Bangladesh and Indonesia.
The meeting took place at the Prime Minister's Office in Tejgaon in the morning.
During the meeting, detailed discussions were held regarding enhancing people-to-people contact, expanding educational linkages and fostering cooperation in the energy sector.
Particular emphasis was placed on the facilities, amenities and safety of the large number of tourists travelling from Bangladesh to Indonesia.
Both sides exchanged views on increasing bilateral trade and creating opportunities for more Indonesian companies to operate in Bangladesh.
Key topics of the meeting included simplifying visa processes, reinstating visa-on-arrival facilities for Bangladeshi citizens and launching direct flights between Bangladesh and Indonesia.
Emphasis was put on leveraging new opportunities for cooperation in potential sectors like trade, investment, energy, tourism, education and people-to-people contact to further deepen the economic and strategic partnership between the two nations.
They also discussed increasing Indonesian investment in Bangladesh and fostering closer ties between the business communities and entrepreneurs of both countries.
Besides, opportunities for expanding trade in ready-made garments, jute, agriculture and palm oil, as well as increasing the export of halal products, were discussed.
Both sides also agreed to strengthen multifaceted cooperation and advance the bonds of shared Muslim brotherhood.
Indonesian Ambassador to Bangladesh Listyowati and Bangladesh Ambassador to Indonesia Md Abul Hasan Mridha were present during the meeting.

item.title: Humaiun: Sincerity needed to resolve water-sharing issues with India
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir on Thursday said sincerity at the political and official levels of Bangladesh and India is essential to finding an amicable resolution to the long-standing water-sharing issues between the two countries.
“If there is sincerity between both countries - at the senior official level, leadership level, and among the water negotiators working from both sides... we have formed a water committee," he told reporters while responding to a question after attending a seminar.
Kobir expressed optimism that the water issues issue could be resolved positively if the leadership of both countries demonstrates the willingness to cooperate.
“If the leadership possesses the mindset to come forward and cooperate, we will certainly achieve an amicable and positive resolution on this issue,” he said.
The state minister said meaningful progress would be possible if there is sincerity between the two countries at all relevant levels, including senior officials, political leadership and water negotiators.
Asked about the broader approach to resolving water-related issues, Kobir said diplomacy and dialogue remain the way forward.
“It is only through discussion, dialogue, and diplomacy that these matters will have to be resolved,” he said.
He also said Bangladesh is taking international law into consideration while dealing with the issues.
“The positions of international law are also being taken into consideration. So, this is where we stand right now,” the state minister said.
Bangladesh and India share 54 transboundary rivers, including the Ganges, Teesta, Brahmaputra, Surma-Kushiyara and Feni, making water management and equitable sharing a key component of bilateral relations.
The Joint Rivers Commission (JRC) serves as the principal bilateral mechanism for discussing shared-river issues.
He said discussions and dialogues on the issues are continuing, with both sides looking into the matters through their respective mechanisms.
“Discussions and dialogues are ongoing and will continue here. From our standpoint, regional cooperation needs to be enhanced,” he told reporters.
The Ganges Water Sharing Treaty, signed in 1996. Bangladesh has been seeking a new arrangement that safeguards its interests, including adequate water flows during the dry season.
The seminar was organised to understand water diplomacy on multilateral platforms and identify potential opportunities for Bangladesh to strengthen its efforts and cooperate with other like-minded countries.
The speakers discussed opportunities for inclusive governance and public-private partnerships in transboundary water management; and amplify youth voices in water justice and explore avenues for integrating youth leadership and participation into transboundary water governance and decision-making processes.

item.title: Home minister: Initiative taken to bring Jungle Salimpur under law and order
item.description:
An initiative has been taken to bring Jungle Salimpur in Chittagong under good governance and discipline, with plans to establish a police academy and relocate Chittagong Central Jail there, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has said.
He made the remarks to journalists at the Secretariat around 3:00pm on Thursday, after a meeting titled “Meeting for the Overall Improvement of Law and Order in Jungle Salimpur, Chittagong.”
The home minister said a decision had been made to establish a police academy in Jungle Salimpur, modeled on Sarda. In addition, 72 acres of land have been acquired in the area to relocate Chittagong Central Jail.
He said government land, hill-category land and khas (state-owned) land in Jungle Salimpur would be brought under good governance. Space has also been allocated for various forces to ensure the permanent presence of law enforcement agencies there.
Highlighting several decisions of the inter-ministerial meeting, Salahuddin said the meeting was attended by representatives of the Ministry of Housing and Public Works, Chittagong Development Authority (CDA), the Divisional Commissioner and Deputy Commissioner of Chittagong, as well as top officials of law enforcement agencies.
Representatives of the Inspector General of Police (IGP), Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB), Armed Police Battalion, Coast Guard and SRB also took part in the meeting.
Salahuddin said the progress of the road network currently being built in Jungle Salimpur was also reviewed at the meeting. Road construction is moving forward in coordination with the Armed Forces Division and under the leadership of the Engineering Construction Battalion (ECB).
The home minister said government land in several mouzas of Jungle Salimpur would be brought under integrated management. A decision has been made to establish a police academy there modeled on Sarda, and the work of identifying land for it is under way.
He said 72 acres of land had been acquired in Jungle Salimpur to relocate Chittagong Central Jail. The jail will be moved to the area beside the Bayezid Link Road.
The home minister also said decisions would be made on the rehabilitation of those who have settled illegally in various parts of Jungle Salimpur. Measures would also be taken regarding the operation of educational and other institutions there.
He said the area would be brought under order by bringing everything under good governance and freeing it from its past as a haven for terror.
The home minister added that, in addition to the police, space had been allocated for the BGB, SRB and Armed Police Battalion to ensure their presence in Jungle Salimpur.
The respective forces will construct facilities on these sites to ensure good governance and law and order in the area.
He said development, government land management, rehabilitation, institutional management and law and order in Jungle Salimpur would be implemented in a coordinated manner.

item.title: CUET standoff persists over demand to reinstate VC
item.description:
The standoff at Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CUET) continued on Thursday, with tensions running high as students, teachers, officers and employees demanded the reinstatement of Prof Dr Abu Sadat Mohammad Sayem as vice-chancellor.
Students locked the university’s main gate and began a sit-in around 9:00am following reports that newly appointed VC Prof Dr Sheikh Shariful Alam might arrive on campus. They chanted slogans and prevented vehicles from entering the university.
However, Prof Shariful had not entered the campus by 3:30pm and was staying at the Chittagong Circuit House.
Meanwhile, teachers, officers and employees staged a sit-in in front of the VC’s office, also demanding Prof Sayem’s reinstatement.
Academic and administrative activities have remained suspended for 17 days amid the protests. Students alleged that the government had yet to take any initiative to resolve the deadlock.
CUET student Abdullah Al Mamun said Prof Sayem had taken several student-friendly initiatives to modernise the university within 56 days of taking office.
“He was removed without any allegation against him. This is unjust. Our movement will continue until he is reinstated,” he said.
Students began protesting on the night of September 21 against the decision to replace Prof Sayem. The following day, they launched a “complete shutdown”, boycotting classes and examinations and holding sit-ins, human chains and signature campaigns. The CUET Teachers’ Association has also expressed solidarity with the movement.
On September 21, the government issued a notification removing Prof Sayem as VC and appointing Prof Dr Sheikh Shariful Alam of Khulna University of Engineering and Technology (KUET) as his replacement.
Prof Sayem was appointed CUET VC on July 27, but was removed just 56 days later, prompting students to launch immediate protests. The ensuing movement has kept the university’s regular academic activities suspended.

item.title: World Egg Day 2026 highlights nutrition, food security
item.description:
World Egg Day 2026 will highlight the nutritional benefits of eggs, their affordability and accessibility, and their role in improving food security and public health, according to a press note by the Bangladesh Poultry Industries Central Council (BPICC) and World's Poultry Science Association (WPSA).
First observed in 1996 following an initiative by the International Egg Commission (IEC) at a conference in Vienna, Austria, the day marks its 30th anniversary this year.
The international theme for 2026 is “Protein That Powers and Protects”, highlighting the role of high-quality protein in eggs in supporting muscle growth, brain development, immune function and healthy ageing. The anniversary mascot, Eggwin, has also been introduced to raise awareness about egg nutrition among people of all ages.
The observance, to be held on Friday, aims to promote eggs as an affordable source of protein and essential nutrients, highlight their importance in meeting the nutritional needs of people of all ages, recognise the contributions of poultry farmers and the industry, and address misconceptions about egg consumption.
Eggs contain high-quality protein and essential nutrients, including choline, iron and vitamin B12, which support muscle development, brain function and overall health.
Choline, found in egg yolks, plays an important role in brain development and nervous system function. Eggs also contain the antioxidants lutein and zeaxanthin, which help protect eye health.
Eggs are widely recognised as an affordable and versatile source of nutrition. Compared with beef and mutton, egg production generally has a lower environmental footprint, making eggs an important protein source in efforts to promote more sustainable food systems.
Poultry farming also contributes to rural livelihoods by providing income and employment for farmers and small-scale producers.
According to the Department of Livestock Services (DLS), Bangladesh produces approximately 24.465 billion eggs annually, averaging more than 60 million a day. Annual per capita egg availability stands at around 137.
The government and relevant agencies are working to increase annual per capita availability to 200 eggs by 2030.
However, rising prices of poultry feed, chicks, medicines and fuel have increased production costs for farmers. Meanwhile, intermediaries and inefficiencies in the supply chain have widened the gap between farm-gate and retail prices, putting pressure on small-scale producers.
Eggs have also been incorporated into the National School Feeding Programme under the Directorate of Primary Education, with two to three eggs a week planned for each student to help address malnutrition and support children's growth and cognitive development.
China is the world's largest egg producer, producing approximately 617 billion eggs annually, according to the information provided in the release.
Mexico leads in per capita egg consumption, with an average of 409 eggs a year. Japan also records high consumption, at around 337 eggs annually.
Annual per capita consumption in many developed countries ranges from 270 to 300 eggs, while availability and consumption in Bangladesh remain comparatively low.
To mark World Egg Day, the Department of Livestock Services, the Bangladesh branch of the World's Poultry Science Association and the Bangladesh Poultry Industries Central Council have jointly taken initiatives to raise awareness about the nutritional value of eggs.
Under the theme “Nutrition in eggs, energy in eggs, and immunity from disease through eggs”, the programs include awareness rallies, seminars and discussions at agricultural universities across the country.
Other activities include distributing free eggs to underprivileged children, orphanages and residents of old-age homes, including in Dhaka, to help improve access to nutritious food.
The initiatives aim to encourage greater awareness of the role of eggs in a balanced diet and highlight the contributions of poultry farmers and the wider industry to food security and nutrition.

item.title: Bus catches fire at Mohakhali terminal
item.description:
A fire broke out in an air-conditioned bus at Mohakhali bus terminal in the capital on Thursday afternoon.
Anwarul Islam Warehouse Inspector at Fire Service & Civil Defence (FSCD) said the fire originated from the bus’s air-conditioning system after it arrived at the terminal from Sherpur around 1:32pm.
Two units from Tejgaon Fire Station rushed to the spot and brought the fire under control at 1:46pm. The fire was completely extinguished at 2:02pm.
The fire might have originated from an electrical malfunction in the bus, the fire service said.
No casualties were reported.

item.title: Driver killed in head-on collision between bus, covered van in Dhamrai
item.description:
A driver was killed in a head-on collision between a bus and a covered van on the Dhaka-Aricha Highway in Dhamrai, Dhaka, on Thursday morning.
The accident occurred around 7:15am in the Srirampur area of the highway.
The deceased was identified as 26-year-old Abu Bakar Siddique, a resident of Netrokona. A bus passenger was also injured in the accident.
According to Fire Service and highway police sources, a Dhaka-bound staff bus of AKH Eco Apparels collided head-on with an Aricha-bound covered van coming from the opposite direction.
The covered van was badly damaged in the collision, and its driver, Abu Bakar, died at the scene.
Personnel from Golra Highway Police Station and the Fire Service went to the scene after receiving the news and recovered the body.
Traffic on the highway was disrupted for some time following the accident but returned to normal after police removed the wrecked vehicles from the road.
Md Zainul, an assistant sub-inspector of Golra Highway Police Station, said the driver’s body had been recovered.
Police are conducting an operation to identify the bus and detain its driver, he said, adding that legal proceedings were underway.

item.title: BB raises foreign travel cash limit to $3,000
item.description:
Bangladesh Bank has raised the limit on foreign currency sales by licensed money changers to outgoing Bangladeshi citizens, allowing travelers to purchase up to $3,000 in cash per instance against their annual personal travel quota.
Under the revised regulations, licensed money changers can now sell up to $3,000 in foreign bank notes and coins to an outbound citizen, increasing the previous single-transaction ceiling of $2,000.
The central bank issued a circular Thursday stating that the policy adjustment aims to better accommodate the foreign currency needs of Bangladeshi citizens traveling abroad.
Under the new measure, travelers can purchase the remaining portion of their allowed annual travel entitlement in other freely convertible and usable currencies—either as notes or coins—subject to overall quota limits and foreign exchange availability.
The updated framework is expected to offer outward-bound citizens greater ease and flexibility when sourcing cash foreign currency through money changers.

item.title: BB issues guidelines for Shariah-based Islamic credit cards
item.description:
Bangladesh Bank has introduced a comprehensive set of guidelines governing the operation of Shariah-compliant Islamic credit cards to ensure strict adherence to Islamic financial principles across commercial banks.
Under the new directives, financial institutions are required to align all products, agreements, transaction processes, fees, charges, and operational workflows with Shariah law.
To replace conventional interest mechanisms, banks must operate under the principles of Qard (interest-free loan) and Ujrah (service fee).
Purchases, cash withdrawals, and utility bill payments made using these cards will be classified as Qard Hasanah (interest-free loans), meaning no additional money, profits, or financial perks can be collected from customers on these transactions.
Furthermore, for cash withdrawals, banks may levy a flat fixed fee, but charging percentage-based fees on the withdrawn amount is strictly prohibited.
The central bank has placed strict restrictions on card usage and operational funding.
Islamic credit cards cannot be used to pay for goods and services prohibited under Islamic law, including alcohol, gambling, and tobacco.
Additionally, banks are forbidden from utilizing funds from Mudaraba deposits or investors' savings accounts to fund credit card operations.
To protect consumer interests, the central bank has made it mandatory for banks to notify cardholders at least 30 days in advance of any changes to card-related fees or charges.

item.title: Bangladesh September PMI sees slight economic contraction
item.description:
The September reading of the Bangladesh Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) fell by 1.3 points from the previous month to 48.6, indicating a slight contraction in overall economic activity.
The Metropolitan Chamber of Commerce and Industry (MCCI), Dhaka and Policy Exchange Bangladesh (PEB) released the PMI September report on Wednesday.
The decline reflected persistent weakness in manufacturing and a return to contraction in construction, while services remained marginally in contraction. Agriculture continued to expand.
The agriculture sector recorded its thirteenth consecutive month of expansion, although the index declined by 1.3 points to 55.2.
New business, business activity and employment recorded slower expansion, while input costs continued to expand strongly despite slight reduction.
Order backlogs remained in contraction, but at a slower rate.
The manufacturing sector declined by 2.6 points to 44.8, recording contraction.
New orders, new export orders, output, stocks of input purchases and finished goods, and imports continued to contract at a faster rate.
Employment reverted to a marginal expansion, while input prices continued to rise.
Order backlogs recorded a strong contraction, while supplier delivery times recorded a slower expansion.
The construction sector returned to contraction after expanding in August, declining by 3.8 points to 48.5.
New business and construction activity contracted, while employment remained unchanged. Input costs continued to expand strongly but at a slight slower rate. Order backlogs reverted to expansion.
The services sector recorded a second consecutive month of marginal contraction, declining by 0.2 points to 49.0.
New business and business activity reverted to contraction, while employment experienced slower contraction.
Input costs expanded strongly while order backlogs remained in contraction.
Respondent feedback for September reflected a cautious and mixed outlook for future business conditions.
Some firms expected activity to improve in the coming months, supported by confirmed orders, reliable buyers and the prospect of stronger seasonal demand during the approaching winter and peak business season.
However, many respondents remained concerned about repeated fuel and oil price increases, rising input and operating costs, weak consumer purchasing power, electricity and gas shortages, and limited access to bank financing.
Several firms also noted that prevailing economic uncertainty made it difficult to plan ahead, with some anticipating further deterioration if fuel prices and other cost pressures continue to rise.
Overall, the feedback indicates that business confidence remains cautious. Future prospects will depend largely on stronger domestic demand, reliable energy supply, improved access to finance and a reduction in cost pressures.
Looking ahead, the Future Business Index indicates expansion across all four sectors, reflecting cautious optimism regarding business conditions.
“The September PMI shows that Bangladesh’s economic dynamism remains under pressure, as weakness in manufacturing, construction and services weighed on overall performance. Agriculture’s continued expansion provides resilience, while slightly positive expectations across all sectors offer a basis for recovery. Strengthening domestic and export demand, ensuring reliable energy supply, easing financing constraints and containing cost pressures will be important to restore momentum,” said M Masrur Reaz, chairman and CEO, Policy Exchange Bangladesh.
The PMI is an initiative that aims to offer timely and accurate insights into the country's economic health to help businesses, investors and policy makers take informed decision.
It was developed by MCCI and Policy Exchange, with support from UK Government and technical support from Singapore Institute of Purchasing & Materials Management (SIPMM).

item.title: Bangladesh, Netherlands discuss trade, migration, regional Issues
item.description:
Bangladesh and the Netherlands on Thursday discussed political and economic developments, the Bangladesh-European Union Free Trade Agreement (FTA), LDC graduation, migration cooperation, human capital development, semiconductor technology, education and sports, and regional and multilateral issues.
The issues were discussed when the Ambassador of the Netherlands to Bangladesh, Joris van Bommel, met State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir at the Ministry in the afternoon.
The Dutch envoy briefed the state minister on the upcoming visit of Minister for Foreign Trade and Development Cooperation of the Netherlands Sjoerd Sjoerdsma, said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
The ambassador congratulated the state minister on his recent assumption of office and expressed confidence in further strengthening Bangladesh-Netherlands relations.
He appreciated the Netherlands’ longstanding support for Bangladesh’s development, particularly in democratic transition, trade and investment, sustainable industrial development, water and agriculture.
The state minister also thanked the Netherlands for its continued support to the Rohingya and host communities and reiterated the importance of safe, voluntary, dignified and sustainable repatriation of the Rohingya to Myanmar.
The ambassador reaffirmed the Netherlands’ commitment to further deepening bilateral cooperation, particularly in water management, agriculture, shipping, maritime infrastructure and people-to-people exchanges.
Both sides underscored the importance of sustained high-level engagement and enhanced cooperation in bilateral and multilateral fora.

item.title: ZCOMMERZ partners with Rajshahi Women Chamber to bring 400 women entrepreneurs online
item.description:
ZCOMMERZ, an e-commerce enablement platform powered by SSLCOMMERZ, has signed a strategic partnership agreement with the Rajshahi Women Chamber of Commerce and Industry (RWCCI) to onboard 400 chamber members onto its platform.
The signing ceremony was held in Rajshahi as part of an initiative to expand digital-commerce opportunities for women entrepreneurs beyond the capital.
ZCOMMERZ has also partnered with the Natore Women Chamber of Commerce and Industry (NWCCI), onboarding 300 of its members onto the platform.
Bangladesh’s digital-commerce ecosystem has more than 300,000 Facebook-based and online businesses, with an estimated 50% operated or co-owned by women.
ZCOMMERZ enables entrepreneurs to establish and manage online stores without coding or technical knowledge. The platform offers product catalogs, order and fulfillment management, customized store links and secure digital payments through SSLCOMMERZ.
The partnership brings RWCCI’s institutional reach together with SSLCOMMERZ’s technology to provide members with professional digital stores and management tools, allowing them to expand beyond local markets.
Raiyan S. Islam, CEO of SSLCOMMERZ, said: “Being the largest online payment enabler of the country, we have a role to play in building a Bangladesh that is digitally savvy, transactionally liberating, and forward-looking. Our long-proven capabilities and cutting-edge innovation brought the answer in a merchant-friendly solution like ZCOMMERZ. We are delighted to onboard RWCCI as a partner in this journey.”
Rosettee Najneen, president of RWCCI, said: “For our members, this is a turning point. Many of our women entrepreneurs have built their businesses on determination alone, without the digital tools to grow beyond their immediate markets. With ZCOMMERZ, they gain a professional storefront, secure payments, and the confidence to sell nationwide. We are proud to bring this opportunity to the women of Rajshahi.”
The signing was followed by a digital-business capacity-building session covering online store creation, product catalog optimization, order tracking, local delivery management, secure digital payments, online-selling safety, and promotion and customer engagement through Facebook and WhatsApp.
Participants also received a live demonstration of ZCOMMERZ and one-on-one onboarding support.

item.title: South Africa host Australia for first time in Tests since sandpaper scandal
item.description:
World Test champions South Africa meet current championship leaders Australia in Durban on Friday at the start of the first Test series between the two countries in South Africa since the controversial ‘Sandpapergate’ tour of 2017/18.
Apart from the scandal of the Australians being caught using sandpaper to alter the condition of the ball, the 2017/18 series was the first won by South Africa on home soil against their arch-rivals in 48 years.
South Africa defeated Australia in the World Test Championship final at Lord’s in London last year but their batting line-up is relatively inexperienced, while their fast bowling stocks have been depleted by what coach Shukri Conrad described as a "pandemic" of hamstring injuries.
Star fast bowler Kagiso Rabada is a particular concern, having not bowled in an official match since May.
He took part in a two-day intra-squad match last weekend and reportedly came through without any problems. Batting coach Ashwell Prince said a final decision on Rabada would be delayed "as late as possible".
The Rabada issue is complicated by the likelihood that South Africa will field two spin bowlers, Keshav Maharaj and Simon Harmer, at a venue which has favoured spin in recent seasons.
This would leave room for only one specialist fast bowler to support left-armer Marco Jansen which would make the team vulnerable to any injury breakdown.
Australia have already ruled out batsmen Josh Inglis with a broken finger and Cameron Green with an abdominal injury.
Australia will also have to make a call on the balance of their attack if the conditions favour spin, although the quartet of captain Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood and off-spinner Nathan Lyon remains intact from the 2017/18 series.
Cummins, Starc and Hazlewood were the beneficiaries of the sandpaper-augmented managing of the ball which enabled sharp reverse swing, particularly in the first Test in Durban, eight years ago, although none has been implicated in the actions that led to lengthy bans for then-captain Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft.
Both camps have been cautious about recalling the events of 2017/18.
"It was a long time ago and I don’t think there is much more to add," Cummins said before the tour.
Conrad said it was not an issue that had been raised in South Africa’s team meetings. "We’re hell-bent on beating them with our skills," said Conrad.
But the coach said he expected South African supporters to remind the Australians of the incident.
"I would like the fans to give them some stick – but respectfully so," said Conrad.

item.title: Former Spurs defender Vega to stand for FIFA presidency
item.description:
Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega has become the first person to announce he intends to run against incumbent Gianni Infantino in the FIFA presidential election next year.
The 55-year-old former Switzerland centre-back has been working in finance since he retired in 2004.
It is not the first time, though, that Vega has announced his intention to run for the top job at world football's governing body.
He had considered running against Infantino following the resignation of Sepp Blatter in the wake of a corruption scandal in 2015.
And he tried to challenge his fellow Swiss in 2022, but failed to garner sufficient support to make it onto the ballot.
"The situation has evolved a lot since then," Vega told AFP, adding FIFA's member associations were "much more open to change" than when he previously sought to stand.
"I am standing because my life has prepared me to serve the game," Vega added in an 11-page dossier announcing his candidacy.
"I believe I have a duty and a social responsibility to protect and defend football -- its integrity, its people and its future."
Pressure has been building on Infantino, who has lost the support of numerous FIFA member associations, since his aborted plan to create a commercial subsidiary to run FIFA's biggest events, such as the World Cup and Club World Cup.
Last week, the Swiss Football Association became the latest to withdraw its support for Infantino, citing concerns over his record on transparency, accountability and institutional responsibility.
"Faith and trust across the football family have been deeply damaged," said Vega in his dossier.
"We must rebuild both, restore FIFA's credibility and reunite the global football family."
It is not clear whether Vega would be able to stand.
He must first gain the backing of at least five of FIFA's 211 member federations, but also be proposed by one of those.
And the rules stipulate a candidate must have been involved in football for two of the previous five years, and pass an eligibility review.
Potential candidates have until November 18 to meet those criteria.

item.title: Messi says already missing playing for Argentina
item.description:
Less than 24 hours after calling time on his international career, Lionel Messi said on Wednesday he was already missing wearing the Argentina jersey.
The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner, who scored a penalty in Tuesday's 3-0 win over Benin in his Buenos Aires swansong, had described the occasion as the "saddest day of my career".
Messi led Argentina to World Cup glory four years ago but his team came under severe criticism for their aggressive style of play during their run to the final in July, when they lost to Spain.
"Yesterday was my last match and I'm already missing the light blue and white jersey," said Messi on social media.
But he added: "I know I'm taking the right decision."
Messi is Argentina's record goalscorer with 126 goals, more than double the next most prolific national team player.
He has won a record number of caps with 208, and his 70 assists for the national team are also the best ever.
"It was an incredible journey, full of joy but also some sorrow," he added, while thanking his family and teammates, and paying tribute to Argentina's other football legend, the late Diego Maradona.

item.title: High school students turn out for new protests across France
item.description:
High school students across France launched a fresh day of protests on Thursday, despite government attempts to ease the crisis which has rocked the country for days.
Students have blocked entrances to hundreds of high schools across the country since late September, and protests have on occasion spiraled into violent clashes with riot police.
Student union leaders urged fresh mobilization across France Thursday, with a rally planned in the capital Paris and national education unions calling a general strike in support.
While many rallies have been peaceful, some demonstrators have started fires, destroyed bus shelters or clashed with riot police -- with unions, rights groups and the children accusing police of using disproportionate force.
In a televised address Wednesday evening, the prime minister Sebastien Lecornu attempted to calm tensions, promising a plan to respond to the crisis by the end of October.
Although Lecornu denied that security forces have “orders to confront” the young people, many students were unconvinced.
Outside one high school in Rennes, around 60 students had already gathered early Thursday.
Hanaa, an 18-year-old student, told AFP she was “disappointed and unconvinced” by Lecornu’s remarks.
“We expected more from him,” agreed fellow student Salyna, 17, who said they were also disappointed the government response would not be announced until the end of the month.
“This is an urgent situation.”
Suzanne Nijdam, president of university student association Fage, said they did not have “even the crumbs of an agreement” after a meeting with the higher education minister Philippe Baptiste.
She called for protests to continue outside high schools and government administrative offices Thursday, with “larger-scale demonstrations next week.”
As the government tried to adopt a conciliatory tone, education minister Edouard Geffray was to visit a high school in Reims and take part in a “dialogue” with students.
And a fresh meeting between the three main student associations with Geffray and Baptiste was planned for Thursday afternoon.
The students have asked for a direct meeting with Lecornu to present what they say are costed proposals to address their demands.
Student demonstrators -- many attending high schools called lycees for children aged between 15 and 18 years old -- have complained of missing teachers, overloaded timetables, dilapidated classrooms and buildings that cannot cope with rising temperatures.
Classes were partially or completely suspended in 375 schools across the country on Thursday morning, according to the education ministry.
At a high school in Paris, AFP saw adult protesters forming a human chain with their arms between police and protesting teenagers, who huddled together carrying backpacks and placards.
Access to the school had been blockaded with bins and railings, and AFP saw some scuffles between riot police and protesters.
In the southern city of Toulouse, high school protesters waved the French flag and placards, while graffiti on a school wall read: “The police are cracking down on France’s children.”
Hundreds of students, police and teaching staff have been injured since the protests began, and more than 6,500 people -- mostly minors -- have been arrested.
A 15-year-old lost a hand on Monday after police fired a stun grenade, and Interior Minister Laurent Nunez told radio broadcaster RTL early Wednesday that he had suspended the police use of stun grenades in response.
Police have opened 18 internal investigations into allegations of misconduct.
The unrest has erupted with just months to go before the 2027 election to choose a successor to centrist President Emmanuel Macron, with far-right veteran candidate Marine Le Pen riding high in the polls despite a graft conviction.

item.title: Trump to give Musk top US science medal
item.description:
President Donald Trump will present close ally Elon Musk and other tech bosses with the top US scientific award at a ceremony on Thursday, the White House said.
Google co-founder Sergei Brin, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and AMD chief Lisa Su will also receive the National Medal of Science at the “Science: A New Golden Age” summit.
Computer mogul Michael Dell and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella will get the National Medal of Technology and Innovation, the top award in its field.
“The Trump Administration is grateful for the contributions of these incredible leaders in science and technology. These recipients are helping ensure America keeps leading the world in innovation,” White House spokeswoman Liz Huston said in a statement to AFP on Wednesday.
Space X and Tesla tycoon Musk has returned to Trump’s good graces after they fell out last year over his role heading the cost-cutting Department of Government Efficiency.
He was also the biggest donor to Trump’s 2024 presidential campaign.
Musk and Huang were both at Trump’s state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping last month.
Along with other tech bosses they were also at the White House last week for talks in which tech chiefs promised to self-regulate against possible threats from artificial intelligence.
Trump has dismissed warnings that AI could wipe out humanity, insisting it is crucial for what he calls the “Golden Age” of the US economy in his second term.
But Trump’s Republican Party could lose control of Congress in midterm elections next month amid voter concerns over the Iran war and the cost of living.

item.title: CARE Bangladesh delegation pays courtesy call on President
item.description:
A delegation of CARE Bangladesh paid a courtesy call on President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir at Bangabhaban on October 6.
The delegation was led by Earl R Miller, former US ambassador to Bangladesh and currently senior strategic adviser, CARE Bangladesh, and Ram Das, country director, CARE Bangladesh, said President's press secretary Md Sarwar Alam.
During the visit, Ram Das shared an overview of CARE’s journey in Bangladesh, which began in 1949.
Since then, CARE Bangladesh has been contributing to the socio-economic development of Bangladesh, including the post liberation war reconstruction, which included the construction of over 85,000 kilometers of rural roads for improved connectivity, while creating employment opportunities for thousands.
Over the following seven decades, CARE gradually expanded into food security and agriculture, health and nutrition, education, women’s economic empowerment, disaster preparedness, climate resilience and women workers skills and well-being in the readymade garment sector.
In the coming days, CARE will strongly focus on agriculture and food security, youth skilling and entrepreneurship and climate resilience.
The President recalled CARE Bangladesh as a popular name in the country and expressed his appreciation for the decades of work in socio-economic development of the country.
He also urged the organization to expand the activities further in the coming days.
Secretaries and senior officials of the President’s Office were present during the meeting.
